title: Screening Ceiling for Re-aged Patient Payment Plans
content:
**Rule.** The longest re-aged schedule of a **Patient Payment Plan** may run past the tier's maximum term only as far as the screening ceiling of the re-aged schedule allows: 60 installments when the open application's household was screened at or below 200 percent of the federal poverty level and 48 installments when it was screened above 200 and at or below 400 percent, each only on tiers whose maximum term is shorter; otherwise the screening ceiling is the tier's maximum term.

**Open application.** A financial assistance application of the patient is open when one of the patient's financial assistance cases in the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care) stands in submitted or pending documents status, a submitted case being taken first. The screening is the household federal poverty level (FPL) percentage recorded on that application in the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care).

| Tier | Tier maximum term | At or below 200% FPL | Above 200% and at or below 400% FPL | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Riverbend Short-Term Payment Plan | 6 | 60 | 48 | 6 |
| Riverbend Standard Payment Plan | 12 | 60 | 48 | 12 |
| Riverbend Extended Payment Plan | 24 | 60 | 48 | 24 |
| Riverbend Long-Term Payment Plan | 36 | 60 | 48 | 36 |
| Riverbend Assistance-Linked Payment Plan | 48 | 60 | 48 | 48 |
| Riverbend Hardship Payment Plan | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 |

**Both sides of each threshold.** Exactly 200 percent takes 60 installments; just above 200 takes 48. Exactly 400 percent takes 48; just above 400 takes the tier's maximum term.
